brief: Goldman's Louis Miller argues the AI pain trade persists because hyperscaler earnings failed to resolve the AI funding and returns debate, keeping risk appetite in non-AI pockets low ahead of the midterms and an Iran decision. Five linked theses follow. First, a Democratic sweep favors Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries, since reauthorized subsidies would improve hospital and insurer earnings, and AI Power, while weighing on ex-Power hardware if datacenter cost-bearing becomes policy. Corporate tax risk is longer-dated: Trump's veto insulates 2027-28 earnings, but a higher rate threatens valuations beyond 2029. Second, demand for AI- and oil-uncorrelated trades is at a high. The revamped Healthcare AI Beneficiaries basket and a Growth/Value systematic rotator, up 27% and 18% year-to-date, lead, and the SPXXAI broadening trade worked in October, though GS flags caution on short-squeeze-driven pockets if growth weakens. Third, underpriced AI disruption has rotated from Software-versus-Semis, already up 88% and re-rated from 17x to 23x forward earnings, into Insurance, pressured by cyber-attack headlines. Fourth, European and Japanese bank underperformance looks overdone: GS likes Greek Banks and expects a BoJ-hike-driven Japan relief rally. Fifth, European Defense's rebound has fundamental support for a possible 30% re-rating if third-quarter results ease execution concerns.
